title: Coherent coefficient calculus with the fixed integral closed structure
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an arbitrary scheme $W$, with independent scheme universe $t$ and coefficient universe $u$. There exist a coefficient derived system calculus $S$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data] and a coherence witness [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] such that its integral closed structure equals $(\mathrm{IntegralOnSlice.duality}\ \ell\ E\ W\ \mathrm{none}).\mathrm{closed}$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. This is equality of the chosen presentations, not an inference of equality from natural isomorphism. No invertibility of $\ell$ on $W$, open immersion, ordinary reduction model, completion model or open comparison is asserted.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 07A4, 08JD (lemma-dual), 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), 0941; presentation-normalization refinement of the coherent coefficient calculus and step 1 of lem-pur-completed-open-tensor-context.

proof.text: Take the coherent coefficient calculus, retaining its reduction/limit adjunction, actual evaluations, strict quotient representatives, fiber Hom and global-section data. Fix the integral closed model to IntegralOnSlice.duality. Fix normalized duality models on the sequence and finite sites as well. Compare old and new tensors as left adjoints to their common internal Hom, and use uncurrying into the fixed K-injective representative to identify the comparison with the identity on actual total-tensor representatives.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 07A4, 08JD (lemma-dual), 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), 0941; presentation-normalization refinement of the coherent coefficient calculus and step 1 of lem-pur-completed-open-tensor-context.

proof.text: Replace the closed fields by the fixed structures and the tensor-model fields by their normalized models. For any old-to-new tensor comparisons a and b, replace a tensor comparison mu for F by F(a inverse);mu;b. Do this also for finite quotient tensor comparisons. Naturality and cancellation prove the finite, evaluation and simultaneous strict-system representative equations using exactly the original chain maps and augmentations. No equality of arbitrary derived system maps is inferred from finite evaluations.

proof.text: The evaluation and transpose identities show that the resulting base-change map equals the old one; thus its naturality, fiber formula and enriched invertibility, and the gamma/projection/H-zero identities, remain valid. For internal composition use the new normalized associators: on three K-flat representatives both composites reassociate the same pure tensors and evaluate phi(psi(x)); localization gives the composition equation. This uses the actual associator normalization, rather than asserting monoidality of an arbitrary adjoint comparison. The mapping-composition equation follows by adjunction naturality. Retain the remaining scalar, resolution and global-limit fields. The integral closed field was assigned the fixed value, so its equality is reflexivity. Zero objects, empty schemes and unbounded representatives are included.

theorem canonicalIntegralEvaluationCalculus :
    ∃ (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
      (_coherence : CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l E W S),
      (IntegralOnSlice.duality l E W none).closed = S.integralClosed
